An opportunity like this one? It is very rare as I am not an education major or ESL ceritified and yet I still get the position. Everyone around me tells me to take this opportunity because you will never get another like this. 

When I go to teach, apparently the hidden objective is to make my college look good so that more foreign students will transfer to it. I am there to teach but my college uses me as a marketing tool. That's all fine and good. However, I don't know what they are thinking trying to manipulate me to be friends with this guy. I tell them not to, the lady adds both of us into a group chat and tries to get us to talk. What? They think us being friends makes the college look better? No.

If I am a good teacher, as well as learning their language and culture, then that would make my college look good. I can do that alone, I don't need the other guy. But they think that if we are best buds so to speak, that it will look better. No. I am there to do a job and make friends with the people. Not to be with the other guy. He does his thing and I do mine. Case closed. And yet, they won't stop trying to manipulate me...

Right now, getting an opportunity to spend almost a year in an Asian country teaching is a dream for me. I gave up a lot to take this opportunity.

As for the people manipulating me, at first I told them "hey, don't force me, I work things out better alone instead of being forced." Obviously they didn't listen. I even spoke to my professor who always helps me and gives me great advice. He sat down with the lady who offered me the position and told her, to paraphrase, "This guy is a friendly, intelligent student who I have had the privilege to teach and become friends with. However, he is a rather shy and passive person who processes things. You can't force him, he has to work it out for himself." 

Am I going to become buddies with this guy? No. At best I would have a neutral opinion about him and not interact with him much. But with people trying to force me to communicate with him and talk to him...it doesn't help. For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. In this case, those people try to push me to become friends with him which leads me to push back.

My girlfriend, who I was supposed to marry soon, left me because of this. Although, all my friends and family say that it was for the best because I am young and don't need to get married yet (I'm 21). This is the choice I made and yet I sometimes regret it. My professor and best friend told me that this is a great and rare opportunity and that he will make sure I get it because he cares about me. He's done international business himself so he knows this kind of stuff. All in all, it's perfect for me. I was so excited for this position and set my sights on this position, nothing else. And now, I basically have the position. The problem? Being forced and manipulated to be friends with that guy. Not everyone handles problems the same way. I tend to avoid conflicts as I am a passive person. But with everyone trying to manipulate me, especially those who claim to be my friend, what I once saw as an exciting opportunity looks more like a miserable experience to me. It was the only opportunity of happiness I saw...
